chains.frame: Which word best describes what the microphone noise did to Zoe’s concert?

beats.text: During Zoe’s otherwise lovely concert, a piercing squeal interrupted the quiet final song and spoiled its ending.
beats.decisive_clue: one harsh interruption spoiled an otherwise good performance
beats.reason: One harsh interruption spoiled an otherwise good performance is the strongest evidence for mar here.

beats.text: The audience applauded warmly afterward, but that ending was still unpleasant.
beats.decisive_clue: one harsh interruption spoiled an otherwise good performance; warm applause afterward does not change that
beats.reason: Applause does not undo the flaw in the concert’s ending, nor make it a lasting injury.

chains.feedback_short: One harsh interruption spoiled an otherwise good performance still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Mar means spoil the appearance or quality of an otherwise good thing; scar means leave a lasting physical mark or deep emotional injury. Applause does not undo the flaw in the concert’s ending, nor make it a lasting injury.
chains.contrast_rule: Mar: single flaw spoils the occasion; scar: mark remains long afterwards.

hints.attention: Think about the quality of that one event.
hints.axis: Mar means spoil an appearance or experience; scar emphasizes a lasting mark or injury that remains.
hints.contrast: Mar: single flaw spoils the occasion; scar: mark remains long afterwards.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what broken glass did to Dev’s wooden table?

beats.text: Broken glass cut a deep white line into Dev’s table, and it remained visible after months of polishing.
beats.decisive_clue: gouge remains on the wood months later
beats.reason: Gouge remains on the wood months later is the strongest evidence for scar here.

beats.text: He tried sanding it again the following year, but the same line could still be seen.
beats.decisive_clue: gouge remains on the wood months later; further evidence: mark remains after another year of repairs
beats.reason: Persistence through repeated repair attempts confirms enduring damage to the surface.
